caveats: DO NOT QUOTE THE ALPHA VALUES. All three are artifacts; -17.3 is the image minimum at the source pixel (-49 sigma). Retained as evidence of the failure, not as measurements.

sigma_alpha uses the local rms of the taylor.0 cutout scaled by the analytic Taylor-1 penalty and the published MT-MFS factor; it is NOT yet an ASKAP-measured injection result. Replacing it is the next increment.
Pulse dilution is not corrected: taylor.1 is fitted over the whole synthesis while the pulse occupies part of it, so alpha here is a synthesis-averaged quantity, not the intrinsic in-pulse index.
A single cutout per term; no independent re-imaging or self-calibration check.
method: Forced value at the catalogue pixel in each Taylor term, local rms from an annulus; alpha = T1/T0. Forced rather than peak-searched, per the stokesv lesson that a peak search over blank sky is biased high.

recover_a_known.conclusion: the anomaly is local to the transient, not a units or scaling error
recover_a_known.test: eight brightest peaks in a 0.25 deg cutout of SB20398, same image as the target

source: RACS/VAST taylor.0 and taylor.1 cutouts staged from CASDA (SODA)
verdict: METHOD INVALID for transients: MFS fits one constant-flux power-law source across the synthesis; an LPT pulse present for part of it cannot be represented, and the deconvolution absorbs the mismatch into taylor.1. See survey/lptspec-findings.md.
